questions.q: Which hormone lowers blood glucose concentration when it rises too high?
questions.explain: Insulin, released by the pancreas, causes cells to take up glucose and the liver to store it as glycogen, lowering blood glucose.

questions.q: Which pair of sex chromosomes is found in a typical human male?
questions.explain: Human males have XY sex chromosomes, while females have XX.

options: A complete lack of a pancreas
Too much insulin being produced from birth
The body's cells no longer responding properly to insulin
questions.explain: In Type 2 diabetes cells stop responding to insulin; it is linked to obesity and often controlled by diet and exercise.

questions.q: How does auxin cause a shoot to bend towards light?
options: Auxin destroys cells on the shaded side
Auxin builds up on the lit side, making it grow faster
Auxin stops all growth on the lit side
Auxin builds up on the shaded side, making those cells elongate more
questions.explain: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side and increases cell elongation there, bending the shoot towards the light.

questions.q: During filtration in the kidney, which substance is NOT normally found in the filtrate of a healthy person?
questions.explain: Large proteins and blood cells are too big to be filtered, so they stay in the blood; glucose is filtered but reabsorbed.

questions.q: Compared with nervous responses, hormonal responses are generally:
questions.explain: Hormonal responses are slower to act but their effects last longer than fast, short-lived nervous responses.

questions.q: An organism with two identical alleles for a characteristic is described as:
questions.explain: Homozygous means having two identical alleles (e.g. BB or bb) for a gene.

questions.q: A homozygous dominant parent (BB) is crossed with a homozygous recessive parent (bb). What proportion of offspring will show the recessive phenotype?
questions.explain: All offspring are Bb (heterozygous), so they all show the dominant phenotype and none show the recessive one.

questions.q: A recessive allele is only expressed in the phenotype when:
options: It is paired with a dominant allele
questions.explain: A recessive allele is only shown when both alleles are recessive, as a dominant allele would mask it.

questions.q: How does meiosis differ from mitosis?
options: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and makes varied gametes; mitosis makes identical diploid cells
Mitosis makes gametes; meiosis makes body cells
questions.explain: Meiosis halves chromosome number to form varied gametes, whereas mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells.
